chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade picking teeth with the reed and the basil stem.

key_terms.يُتَخَلَّلَ: to pick teeth / use a toothpick

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia ruling on using reed and basil stems as toothpicks?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) specifies the prohibition of using reed (*qasab*) and basil (*rayhan*) stems for *siwak*, distinguishing them from the preferred date-palm or olive wood. Shia jurists often interpret this restriction not as a blanket ban on all plant materials, but as a precaution against ritual impurity (*najāsah*) or specific hygienic properties of these particular plants, reflecting the detailed attention to oral hygiene in Shia fiqh.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> forbade picking teeth with the reed and the basil stem’.
en.sarwar: 10. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Dihqan from Durust from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said

the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, would use for a toothpick all kinds of wooden fragments except the leaves of palm trees and reeds.’”
